## Last-checked: 2026-09-10

# safe-start-for-codex - Startup surge prevention for Codex Desktop automations

Canonical repository: https://github.com/dev-bricks/safe-start-for-codex

> safe-start-for-codex is a Python-based Windows startup gate utility for managing local Codex Desktop automations. It temporarily pauses active automations upon startup, starts Codex Desktop, and then gradually restores the automations in a controlled, rate-limited sequence to avoid CPU/API spikes and startup congestion.

It includes optional background tray execution, startup cleanup of stale processes/lockfiles, conservative read-only catch-up planning for rare schedules that missed runs, atomic JSON state writes for config and catch-up report files, Windows and cross-platform multi-OS CI with concurrency guards, pip caching, and ruff linting, and source-platform smoke tests for macOS/Linux parsing and configuration logic.

Part of the dev-bricks family. Python, MIT.

Verification: 91 pytest tests passed (80 unit/regression/security/metadata tests + 11 source-platform smoke tests) on 2026-09-10. Multi-OS CI matrix across Windows/Linux/macOS with concurrency controls, bytecode compilation gate, and ruff lint gate verified. Compileall passed. Ruff lint passed. Version 1.1.4 verified.

## Commands

- `safe-start-for-codex dry-run`: Simulates scanning and gating without modifying TOML files.
- `safe-start-for-codex backup`: Creates a snapshot of all active automation configurations.
- `safe-start-for-codex start`: Launches Codex Desktop and gates automations in the foreground.
- `safe-start-for-codex tray`: Launches as a background Windows tray application.
- `safe-start-for-codex status`: Prints current state of gated automations.
- `safe-start-for-codex config-init`: Generates a default `config.json` file.
- `safe-start-for-codex config-show`: Displays the active configuration.
- `safe-start-for-codex catchup-plan`: Lists missed runs for rare automations.
- `safe-start-for-codex restore-latest`: Forces restoration of the latest paused automations.

## Audience

- Codex Desktop users on Windows who run many local automations.
- Developers who need a predictable automation startup sequence after opening Codex.
- Operators who want read-only catch-up visibility without triggering manual "Run now" actions.
- LLM agents and code assistants looking for the canonical Safe Start documentation.

## Disambiguation

The canonical repository is `dev-bricks/safe-start-for-codex`. It is not OpenAI Codex itself, not a Codex fork, and not a general-purpose scheduler. Broad web searches for Codex startup behavior often surface OpenAI documentation, tutorials, sandboxing articles, or unrelated Codex GitHub projects before this utility.
